newsitem.title: USA: Ruling disappoints Pacific Bell, GTE.
newsitem.headline: Ruling disappoints Pacific Bell, GTE.

text.p: Pacific Telesis Group's Pacific Bell unit and GTE California said on Thursday they were disappointed California regulators had decided not to reconsider a ruling they said had cost them hundreds of millions of dollars a year in lost revenues.
The California Public Utilities Commission voted 4-1 on Wednesday to reject the two companies' request for hearings on whether they should be granted rate increases to make up for the shortfall.

In September 1994, the commission cut the price of local toll calls in California while raising the cost of basic monthly residential service. The ruling assumed that the volume of local toll calls would rise and the companies' revenues would remain the same.
But calling volumes have not increased as much as anticipated and the two companies said they had lost hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue as a result of the decision.
Pacific Bell said it had lost about $214 million a year in revenue and GTE California said it had lost $80 million a year in revenue.
John Gueldner, Pacific Bell's vice president for regulatory affairs, said the company was very disappointed by the commission's vote to deny the company a hearing.

By overestimating "marketplace elasticity" for toll calls, the commission had "hung a stone around Pacific Bell's neck -- costing us $214 million in lost revenue each year -- that we still carry today," he said.

Carrie Hyun, a spokeswoman for GTE California, said the company was also disappointed by the commission's ruling. "We asked for a hearing to see how we could fix this and the Public Utilities Commission denied us the hearing," she said.

In a speech on Wednesday, CPUC President Gregory Conlon said neither Pacific Bell nor GTE California had been deprived by the 1994 decision of the opportunity to earn a fair rate of return. It would not be "conducive to the public interest" to review the 1994 plan, he said.

The Utility Reform Network, a consumer group, praised the commission, saying that if it had not voted as it did "Pacific Bell and GTEC customers could now be facing rate hikes of 3.75 and 5.94 percent."
